page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.2xlarge is an entry-tier, compute-leaning virtual machine belonging to the shared instance family. Powered by the KVM hypervisor on an x86_64 architecture, it features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. Memory capacity is fixed at 16.0 GB, providing 2.0 GB per vCPU. The instance contains no dedicated hardware accelerators or GPUs, does not bundle local storage, and connects via a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps.

Benchmark results highlight clear tradeoffs associated with the shared-core allocation and processor generation. Single-threaded capabilities are modest, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 908.0 and a stress-ng single-core rating of 1093.09. However, aggregate compute performance scales to average levels, reaching 8030.46 in multi-core stress-ng tests and a PassMark CPU score of 8828.45. Memory subsystems deliver read bandwidth of 60.46 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 45.41 GB/sec on large 256MB blocks, though data-intensive and single-thread compression workloads remain relatively slow.

Given its shared resource model, the instance provides cost-effective access to multi-threaded execution environments without the overhead of dedicated hardware. Workload fits include background batch tasks, static web serving, Clang compilation, microservices, and general entry-level development environments that do not require high single-thread clock speeds, local high-speed disk arrays, or dedicated compute isolation.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.n4.2xlarge is a shared compute instance providing 8 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM on an x86_64 architecture powered by an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. It operates across 4 physical cores using hyper-threading, without local storage or GPU hardware, and provides a 1 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark evaluations reveal conservative single-core output alongside moderate multi-threaded capacity, scoring 8030.46 in stress-ng multi-core testing and 8828.45 on the PassMark CPU suite. Memory operations provide large-block uncached read and write speeds of 60.46 GB/sec and 45.41 GB/sec, respectively. Due to its shared vCPU allocation, the instance functions as a cost-conscious option for multi-threaded batch operations, development environments, and static web serving.
